_protocol: Direction-1b two-stage arm at MATCHED training strength: stage 1 = full-population grouped-OOF bank prediction (recomputed from scratch under the frozen Layer-1 protocol, NOT read from the discarded results/*_va_nl_oof_*.npy); stage 2 on E = 2-column logistic combiner [bank_oof, dense_prob] with GroupKFold(5) OOF, against a [bank_oof]-alone combiner as calibration control. Group-level paired bootstrap, 2000 draws.
_why: the E-refit VAT stack is fitted on ~20% of the rows the fullfit bank sees, so 'fused vs bank' at E-refit footing is not a like-for-like comparison; 1b is.

_platform_caveat: This recompute ran on macOS/arm64 while the PUBLISHED Layer-1 numbers were produced on sk3 (linux/x86-64). GroupKFold orders group sizes with an UNSTABLE np.argsort, so ties among equal-sized groups break differently across sort kernels and the FOLD ASSIGNMENT itself differs by architecture (verified independently by the VAT-stack agent: byte-identical matrices, md5-equal sklearn 1.8.0, numpy pinned to 2.2.6 -- fold fingerprint still differed, aops VA_lin .77116 sk3 vs .76922 mac). CONSEQUENCE: absolute levels here may differ from the sk3-published values by ~.002-.007, so the reproduction gate is read with that slack. The D1b CONTRAST is unaffected: bank-alone and bank+T combiners are fitted on the SAME folds in the SAME process, so the paired delta and its bootstrap are internally valid. Only cross-machine absolute comparisons need the sk3 re-run.
